answer: An atlas office hands each agent one inlet to map. The agent walks the shore at low tide, sets ember red stones beside tide pools, and draws the pools into the atlas page with the date and key beside it. A second agent walks that inlet the next week and checks every stone against the page, signing only pools that match. A page with no matching stones for two tides loses its name, and a second key on the same inlet voids both. A thousand fake names need a thousand walked inlets, a thousand painted stones, and a thousand checkers walking mud at low tide.
